A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OlaBench/OlaMind work. The complete main texts and Appendices A–G, including tables, equations and figures, support reliable comparison across repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, human validation, online A/B results and appendix analyses across service intents.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds proprietary-model evaluations and controlled ablation results.

M1.justification: The thought-restructuring stages, SFT/GRPO pipeline, reward terms, Algorithm 1 and hybrid-CoT inference are retained. Additional descriptions of rubric selection, judge tuning and post-CoT prompting document implementation details without establishing a revision of the underlying method.

E1.justification: OlaBench-Core/Risk/Hall, the RAG/workflow/agent scenarios, community support, livestream interaction and appendix intent coverage are unchanged. The additional models and ablations use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Proprietary Model-A and the Model-B base-model comparison while retaining existing comparators. New Table 5 substantially broadens training-method comparisons with RFT using LLM CoT, human-reply-only SFT and single-stage RL, beyond v2's checkpoint comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds a third backbone and controlled reward-removal, reasoning-supervision and single-stage training conditions, substantially expanding the evaluation design. Online evaluation also adds average session turns. The service judge is now reported as Proprietary Model-B rather than Doubao-Seed-1.6; whether this represents anonymization or substitution, and whether evaluations were rerun, is unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's stage comparisons, rubric reward curves and risk/case analyses, new Table 5 tests six reward removals, alternative reasoning supervision and staged versus single-stage RL. These directly examine central design choices that lacked corresponding controlled comparisons in v2.

E5.justification: A/B p-values, human–LLM agreement reporting and reward-statistics plots are retained. The added results introduce no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds proprietary-model results, including Model-B Stage-2 at 83.64; the earlier headline score of 78.72 remains in the unchanged Qwen3-14B row. Table 5 adds ablation outcomes, Figure 4 adds Model-B's 2.6× speedup, and Section 5.2 newly reports over 20% fewer online session turns. The new ablation prose reports 27.7% hallucination without its reward, whereas Table 5 reports 32.7%.

T1.justification: The length-penalty definition in Equation 1 and mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The benchmark and training contributions, superiority over GPT-5.2/Gemini 3 Pro, and deployment-benefit claims retain their meaning and scope. The updated headline score reflects an added backbone rather than a redefined scientific contribution.

C2.justification: The new ablation discussion explains reward complementarity, advantages of expert-strategy supervision and exploration as a diverse behavioral prior. Appendix F adds a single-model-bias rationale for rubric construction. Existing limitations concerning generalization, computational overhead and text-only coverage remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project/evaluation link, the Volcengine Ark platform, hallucination-judge LoRA settings and reference-generation/selection details. It clarifies post-CoT latency timing and business-cycle coverage of online testing. Conversely, the previously named service judge becomes anonymous Model-B without an identity mapping.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hu et al. (2022) for LoRA and revises the reference supporting TeleEval-OS. The broader related-work discussion and positioning of OlaBench and OlaMind remain stable.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization is retained. Changes comprise a new ablation subsection, focused method and implementation explanations, abstract edits, and small language/formatting corrections, including the malformed response label in the RAG example.

P2.justification: v3 adds an ablation table and radar figure, expands Table 3 and the Pareto plot, and adjusts Figure 1 styling. Existing risk, reward and conversation figures are retained, with appendix renumbering and reflow within the same overall layout.

improvement.justification: New Table 5 provides more direct evidence for the central training choices than v2's checkpoint comparisons, while added implementation and latency details improve interpretability. These benefits are tempered by anonymous key models, unclear continuity of the evaluation judge, and the new 27.7% versus 32.7% text/table inconsistency. The higher headline score comes from another backbone and does not itself establish improved paper quality.
